public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI is taking on about $1.4 trillion in obligations against roughly $13 billion in revenue.

statement.excerpt: A few days ago, Sam Altman got seriously pissed off when Brad Gerstner had the temerity to ask how OpenAI was going to pay the $1.4 trillion in obligations he was taking on, given a mere $13 billion in revenue.
statement.document_title: OpenAI probably can’t make ends meet. That’s where you come in.

our_interpretation: Assess the financial comparison, not the description of Altman's emotions.
The reference period is the late-October interview and the days immediately preceding the post.
Obligations means announced multiyear infrastructure commitments, not necessarily recognized debt or expenditure already incurred.
The revenue figure lacks a reporting period and does not distinguish realized revenue, a full-year projection, or an annualized run rate. These measures cannot be substituted for one another.
The single contract metric_scope describes the revenue denominator. The commitments component has a separate scope in its evidence item.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous records establish approximately $1.4 trillion in infrastructure commitments and approximately $13 billion in revenue on an identifiable, consistent reporting basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish a materially different commitments total or revenue figure for the period and measure actually asserted.
